first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A Portugal wedding guide from a planning service: pick a region, check the legal rules for your passport, then talk to one 'Wedded Advisor' who plans it. No price up top, which I actually prefer to a fake 'from' number. What I can't tell in five seconds is what the advisor costs me or why I'd use them instead of emailing a quinta myself.

attention_map.quote: Get Married in Portugal, from a Sintra Palace to an Algarve Cliff
attention_map.why: Clear about where and what. The quick answer giving 'at least one month before the date' from the government site, plus the line that many couples marry legally at home and do a symbolic ceremony in Portugal, is straight talk. No price in the hero means no bait.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until sign-off: a non-numeric line naming Wedded Concierge and one Wedded Advisor, or hide the strip.
attention_map.why: So the proof bar is either gone or just says your own brand name back to me. Not having fake numbers is better than having them, but it leaves me with nothing to go on.

attention_map.quote: What can couples see and do in Portugal that no other country offers?
attention_map.why: 'No other country offers' is the kind of line I tune out. The sights themselves are fine but this is the brochure bit, I scroll past it.

attention_map.quote: Each card has the same labelled lines in order: Setting; Best months; Nearest airport (code); Guests.
attention_map.why: If 'Best months' is the same national answer on all five cards and 'Guests' is blank or 'Ask your Wedded Advisor', the cards only really differ by airport code. I can't compare regions like for like on the one thing I need, which is whether my guest count fits.

attention_map.quote: Queluz and the National Palace of Sintra can be needed for state events, and events on those dates may have to be cancelled
attention_map.why: This is the catch, told to me before I have to dig for it. Same with the Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027. This is the most believable part of the whole page. It does sit a bit awkwardly next to an H1 selling me 'a Sintra Palace'.

attention_map.quote: a permit from the local council or port authority
attention_map.why: Specific, names who gives the permit. Better than the vague 'extra permits' everyone else writes.

attention_map.quote: Exclusivity can mean paying for unoccupied rooms; a buy-out is often separate from the venue fee
attention_map.why: Finally someone talks about the hidden costs on the venue side and tells me to check whether quotes include VAT. That's useful. But it's all 'can', 'often', 'may' and no numbers, so I know what to fear, not what it costs.

attention_map.quote: Legal and cost details checked October 2026, with sources named in each tab.
attention_map.why: Dated, sourced, split by Australian, US and UK passport. This is the bit I'd actually use, and it's the part the other tabs I have open get wrong or skip.

attention_map.quote: Fallback until then: explain what drives cost (guest count, region, season, nights at the venue, exclusivity) with no figures, and offer a Wedded Advisor estimate.
attention_map.why: If the cost table isn't signed off I get a list of 'things that affect price' and a nudge to call. That's the classic 'call us for pricing' move. Even if the EUR 25,000 to 70,000 table does show, it's someone else's numbers, not yours.

attention_map.quote: Frame as what a weekend can include, planned by Wedded Concierge, not as a package inclusion list or price
attention_map.why: Welcome dinner, ceremony, brunch, 'an on-the-day coordinator'. Nice picture, but 'can include' with no price is not an inclusions list. I can't tell what's in and what's extra.

attention_map.quote: hidden at launch: only 2 Portugal real weddings
attention_map.why: So there is no evidence on the page that you've done a wedding in Portugal at all. Hiding two is your call, but from my side it reads as zero.

attention_map.quote: otherwise say a Wedded Advisor explains fees in your currency on the first call
attention_map.why: This is the dealbreaker line. What does the concierge charge, is it a fee, a commission, a markup on the venue? 'We'll explain on the call' is exactly what people say before the upsell. And 'Why book through Wedded Concierge rather than the venue directly?' is answered only from 'approved service facts', which so far is 'one Wedded Advisor'. That is not a reason.

attention_map.quote: Is a wedding in Portugal cheaper than at home?
attention_map.why: If the answer has no comparison it'll be a non-answer. Rest of the FAQ looks like it repeats the legal tab, which is fine because at least it should say the same thing.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links on a page I'm using to make a serious money decision. Makes the site feel like a magazine, not a planner.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price at all ('No Wedded Wonderland figure and no From AUD price on this page'), and s6 is explicitly 'not as a package inclusion list'. The venue charges box warns about buy-outs and VAT, but nothing tells me what Wedded Concierge's own service includes or excludes, or what it costs.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: The legal timing is the same everywhere ('at least one month', 'up to six months', 'one source of truth per fact id'). The beach permit wording is the same in the card and FAQ. Small wobble: the H1 sells 'a Sintra Palace' while the palace strip says Monserrate is under scaffolding and Queluz can be cancelled. Region cards say guests nothing while the qualifier asks me my guest count.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: Proof strip is hidden or non-numeric until sign-off, real weddings block 'hidden at launch', founder quote removed, no named venues. Nothing on the page shows a wedding you have actually run in Portugal.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: The page itself is the best argument: passport-specific legal steps, palace conditions, venue charge traps. But the direct answer in s10 is limited to 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' with 'no capability claims'. No fee transparency, no stated benefit like better rates or Wedded Privileges specifics for Portugal ('no Portugal hotel names until confirmed').

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'an on-the-day coordinator' in a list of what a weekend 'can include'. The brief itself says s10 covers this 'only with an approved service line', which doesn't exist yet. Nothing on backup plans, rain (despite listing 'heavy rain October to February'), or a palace event being cancelled for a state event.

objections_triggered.triggered_by: Guests line: ... Leave it out of the cards (or 'Ask your Wedded Advisor')

trust_signals_noticed: Palace conditions spelt out: state-event cancellations, nothing fixed to heritage, Monserrate scaffolding to Q1 2027
Venue charge traps named: unoccupied rooms under exclusivity, separate buy-out, per-guest minimums, check VAT
Legal rules split by Australian, US and UK passport, with government sources linked
Planning timeline separates the official one-month minimum from advice
No fake from price and no made-up numbers in the proof strip
Honest that there are no Portugal packages, a planned weekend instead
turn_offs_noticed: 'that no other country offers' framing in the spotlight section
Celebrity trending links (Ronaldo, Perrie Edwards) on a planning page
Lots of 'can', 'may', 'often' and 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' fallbacks: honest, but it adds up to a page that keeps sending me to a call
'Start for free' guest website button: makes me wonder what the paid version is

emotional_response.overall: Grudging respect. This is more upfront about the catches than the other three tabs I have open, but it goes quiet exactly where my money is involved.
emotional_response.anxiety: Fear of being upsold on the first call is not addressed at all.

payload.decision_reason: I'll bookmark it for the legal-by-passport tab and the palace and venue charge warnings, which are better than anything else I've got open. I won't enquire, because I still don't know what Wedded Concierge charges or what's included, and there is zero proof you've done a wedding in Portugal. 'We'll explain fees on the first call' is the line that stops me.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, credit where it's due: you told me the palace can get cancelled for a state event and that exclusivity means paying for empty rooms. Nobody else did. But what's the catch with you? There's no price, no list of what you do and don't cover, no weddings you've actually done here, and the answer to 'what do you charge' is 'we'll tell you on the call'. I'm comparing three other services this week. The ones that tell me their fee win.
